text:
Dmitry Orlov's verdict on his start, in a Sharks Hockey Digest headline this month: "I'm Not Really Happy." It's not hard to see why. San Jose takes only 41% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, and his ice time has dropped by more than two minutes a night over his last ten games.

The points tell a kinder story: seven in those ten games, ten on the season, six of them on the power play. That's where his value has always been. Evolving-Hockey had him at 0.2 wins above replacement last season, with the power play (+4.8 goals) carrying almost all of it, and his shot still sits near the top of the league by speed. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with stopping 15% of the entries aimed at him, so the defending isn't as bad as the on-ice numbers suggest; he's playing on a team that gives up more chances than anyone. For the Sharks, the question is whether he's a power-play specialist or still a second-pair defenceman.
